newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Tractor seen to raise HK$1.2 bln max. in IPO.
newsitem.headline: First Tractor seen to raise HK$1.2 bln max. in IPO.

text.p: First Tractor Co Ltd, a Chinese agricultural tractor maker and assembler, is expected to raise HK$936 million to HK$1.19 billion by seeking an H-share listing in Hong Kong in June, analysts said.

The agricultural tractor maker and assembler is expected to issue 300 million H-shares, or 40 percent of its enlarged share capital, at price ranging from HK$3.12 to HK$3.97 each, analysts said after attending a company presentation on Thursday.
H-shares are Chinese enterprises shares listed in Hong Kong.
The issue price will represent a prospective price to earnings multiple of 9.45 to 11.48 times on a fully-diluted basis and 8.1 to 10.31 times on a weighted average basis.
Of the total, 255 million shares will earmark for international placement, and 45 million shares will be offered to the Hong Kong investors by public offering, analysts said.
The company parent China First Tractor, a state owned enterprise of Henan Province, will hold 60 percent of the stake following the listing, they said.
First Tractor is also expected to grant underwriters an option to require the company to issue an additional 45 million new shares to cover overallotment, they added.
The issue price is expected to be fixed on June 8, Hong Kong public offering will run from June 11 to 16 and dealing in the company shares is expected to begin on June 23, analysts said.
Peregrine Capital is expected to be the sponsor of the issue, they said.
Analysts said the company is expected to use the proceeds to expand its manufacturing capacity to meet the growing domestic demand for tractors, to reduce debt and for working capital.

The company posted a profit of 181.1 million yuan for the year ended in December 1996, up from 119.5 million yuan in 1995. Turnover was 3.01 billion yuan in 1996, compared with 2.22 billion yuan in 1995, sources said.

First Tractor has estimated its profit after taxation of about 253 million yuan for the year ending in December 1997, compared with 175 million yuan profit in 1996, 100 million yuan in 1995 and about just one million yuan in 1994, analysts said.
Turnover has increased to 3.0 billion yuan in 1996, from 2.20 billion in 1995 and 1.30 billion in 1994, they said.
